description: Map Cowrie honeypot JSON events onto the ECS-style honeypot-events mapping

script.description: Flatten Filebeat's nested 'cowrie.*' namespace (see infra/filebeat/filebeat.yml) onto the document root, then drop the now-empty 'cowrie' container. No-op when 'cowrie' is absent, e.g. when a document is fed to this pipeline directly at root level (as backend/tests/test_ingest_pipeline.py does). This is the single place field policy lives: known fields get renamed below, known noise gets removed below, and anything left over is neither, so Elasticsearch's dynamic:strict mapping rejects it by name instead of it silently vanishing.
script.source: if (ctx.containsKey('cowrie')) { for (entry in ctx.cowrie.entrySet()) { ctx[entry.getKey()] = entry.getValue(); } ctx.remove('cowrie'); }

remove.description: Telnet option negotiation (WILL/DO NAWS...) is protocol noise, first seen on the live honeypot 2026-10-18. Removed ONLY on this event type, so a future event whose `command` means something is still refused by the strict mapping rather than silently dropped.
Cowrie's flag for a download that finished after its session closed. Seen on the live honeypot 2026-10-18; no analytical use. Download events only, like the telnet fields above.

rename.description: Cowrie's own reason string: why a download failed (e.g. 'TFTP: Transfer timed out'; downloads are blocked on the live VM), or why a Telnet connection was dropped (e.g. a port scanner's non-Telnet bytes, first seen 2026-10-19 on the GCP evaluation Cowrie). Only these event types and only a STRING: Filebeat reports a malformed log line as an `error` OBJECT, which must keep failing loudly.
Cowrie stamps every event with ssh or telnet. This used to be removed as noise, so every telnet session was labelled ssh by the default below.

geoip.description: Country of the source address, into the already-mapped source.country (no template change, so no index needs new mappings). Country only: city-level lookups on attacker infrastructure are precise-looking and frequently wrong. Skipped when a country is already present, so a document that arrives with one keeps it. ignore_failure: an address the database cannot place stays unplaced; it is never a reason to reject the event. Private addresses simply resolve to nothing.

script.description: LOAD-BEARING under dynamic:strict. Until Elasticsearch has downloaded the GeoLite2 database -- lazily, after this pipeline is first installed, and never on an offline machine -- the geoip processor tags EVERY document '_geoip_database_unavailable_GeoLite2-Country.mmdb' in a 'tags' field this mapping does not have, so every event would be rejected at index time and ingest would stop. Only that processor's own tags are removed; any other 'tags' still fails loudly, as unmapped fields should. Verified with _simulate on 8.15 with no database present.
script.source: ctx.remove('tmp_geo'); if (ctx.tags instanceof List) { ctx.tags.removeIf(t -> t instanceof String && t.startsWith('_geoip_')); if (ctx.tags.isEmpty()) { ctx.remove('tags'); } }

rename.description: The HTTP honeypot (infra/webpot). After the url -> file.url rename above, which must never see this object.

script.description: Derive event.category and event.outcome from event.action
script.source: def a = ctx.event?.action; if (a == null) { return; } if (a.contains('session.connect') || a.contains('session.closed') || a.contains('client.')) { ctx.event.category = 'network'; } else if (a.contains('login.')) { ctx.event.category = 'authentication'; ctx.event.outcome = a.contains('success') ? 'success' : 'failure'; } else if (a.contains('command.')) { ctx.event.category = 'process'; ctx.event.outcome = a.contains('failed') ? 'failure' : 'success'; } else if (a.contains('file_download') || a.contains('file_upload')) { ctx.event.category = 'file'; } else if (a.startsWith('web.')) { ctx.event.category = 'web'; } else { ctx.event.category = 'other'; }

remove.description: Known-noise Cowrie fields with no mapped ECS home. Live for both the direct/_simulate path (root-level docs, e.g. backend/tests/test_ingest_pipeline.py) and the Filebeat path (flattened from 'cowrie.*' by the script processor above). 'uuid'/'width'/'height'/'duration_ms' were the fields that originally tripped strict_dynamic_mapping_exception under live Cowrie traffic; 'duplicate'/'name'/'value'/'size' are additional known-noise fields from cowrie.session.file_download/file_upload, cowrie.client.var, and cowrie.log.closed. Deliberately NOT included: 'error' (written by Filebeat's ndjson parser on a malformed log line) — that must keep failing loudly via strict_dynamic_mapping_exception rather than being suppressed here.
